text:
maya: Quick heads-up — I'm running a small demo tomorrow of an ephemeral API key provisioning flow for the sampleapp. Want to validate env var UX + rotation edgecases. anyone free to poke at it?

devon: I can join for 30 mins after lunch. is this the flow where the app requests a short-lived key from the control plane and injects it into the container?

maya: yup. flow is: user logs in -> sampleapp calls /v1/auth/issue-ephemeral with project scope -> control plane returns key + TTL -> app writes to /run/redwood/creds and sets REDWOOD_API_KEY env for child processes. rotation done via sidecar that renews before TTL-10s.

sam: sounds fine. two quick asks: 1) how do we surface failure modes in the app logs (e.g., auth denied, network timeout), 2) what's the backoff/ retry logic on renewals?

maya: good Qs. I added a minimal log line on failures but it's terse. renewals use exponential backoff with jitter up to 30s, then we escalate to fallback: switch to long-lived project token pinned via k8s secret if available.

liz: curious about env var convention: REDWOOD_API_KEY vs RW_API_KEY vs RW_EPHEMERAL_KEY. Any reason to pick one over another? Sampleapp currently uses REDWOOD_API_KEY.

ben: prefer explicit name like RW_EPHEMERAL_KEY to avoid collisions with users who already set REDWOOD_API_KEY for other tooling. also makes it clear it's short-lived.

devon: +1 for RW_EPHEMERAL_KEY but maybe keep backward compatibility: if REDWOOD_API_KEY is present, don't overwrite unless `--force`?

maya: plan: write to RW_EPHEMERAL_KEY, and if only REDWOOD_API_KEY exists then log a warning and honor existing value. If both present, prefer RW_EPHEMERAL_KEY.

sam: edgecase: what if process A reads env at startup and spawns child processes; rotating env var won't update already-running children. how are we handling that for sampleapp?

maya: currently sidecar also writes creds to filesystem at /run/redwood/creds and we provide a tiny helper that returns a socket path for retrieving current token — apps can fetch on demand instead of relying only on env. demo shows both approaches.

ben: can we show a quick example for container startup in README? e.g.
```
# init container copies shim and starts sidecar
RW_EPHEMERAL_KEY="" \ 
  /usr/local/bin/redwood-sidecar --project myproj --socket /run/redwood/agent.sock &
# app uses helper to get token at runtime
TOKEN=$(redwood-cred-get --socket /run/redwood/agent.sock)
export RW_EPHEMERAL_KEY="$TOKEN"
exec ./app
```

maya: yes, added that snippet to the demo README. also added a fallback CLI `redwood-cred-get --env` that will print export lines for shells.

infra-bot: deploy:demo-ephemeral-key-flow succeeded in staging (build 3837). :white_check_mark:

devon: tried the staging image, saw renewals happening but hit an auth denied once when control plane returned 401 for a rotated key — should we log the full request id so support can trace?

maya: good catch. I'll add request_id to error logs and a user-facing error code like ERR_EPHEMER_AUTH_DENIED so we can correlate.

sam: also add a non-fatal metric for "renewal_failures" with labels {project, node_pool} so SRE can alert on spikes.

maya: doing that. Also thinking about the UX for SDKs: the JS/py SDKs should expose a helper that can either read from env or call the sidecar socket. want parity across SDKs.

ben: SDK parity note: make the helper surface a simple interface: getToken(options) where options.socket or options.envName. Then libs can default to socket first, env fallback.

liz: onboarding friction: for local dev we should provide a lightweight dev agent that issues 24-hour ephemeral tokens and writes to env automatically so new users don't have to create k8s secrets.

maya: yep there's `redwood dev-agent --ttl 24h` in the demo. It prints export commands you can source.

devon: tiny nit: on macOS Docker for Mac, mounting /run can be funky. maybe support specifying alternative cred dir via REDWOOD_CRED_DIR env and document it.

maya: added REDWOOD_CRED_DIR override to README and the sidecar honors it. thanks.

sam: one more: rotation race conditions — if two nodes renew the same project token concurrently, control plane should avoid issuing duplicate overlapping tokens or at least return an idempotency key. Is that supported?

maya: control plane currently accepts idempotency keys; sampleapp will pass node_id as idempotency_key. if the control plane detects duplicate renewals it'll return the existing token until TTL-5s. I'll surface that behavior in the demo notes.

ben: let's run the demo at 2pm, I can bring a checklist: env var naming, socket helper, fallback policy, log codes, metrics, local dev agent.

maya: great — scheduled 2pm. If you want to try earlier, staging link: https://staging.redwood.example/demo/ephemeral (credentials in 1password).

devon: :thumbsup: I skimmed the README and left one comment on the PR about the helper API naming.

maya: thanks all — appreciate the quick reviews.

infra-bot: reminder: demo branch will auto-delete in 7 days unless flagged for retention.

liz: :party-parrot: excited to see this in docs for new-hire onboarding."
